research_question: Would copying local model files to a RAM disk remove physical disk reads during generation?

synapse_inspected_read_only.linux_ram_display: Physical occupancy including cached pages, with OS availability and cache reported separately.
synapse_inspected_read_only.linux_disk_read_display: Backend /proc/<pid>/io physical read_bytes deltas, not cached read syscall bytes or PCIe transfers.

storage_inspection.caution: These are current resolved mounts, not a claim about historical NVMe benchmark storage.

file_cache_evidence.method: Read-only fincore --bytes --json before and after the controls.
file_cache_evidence.page_rounding_note: Resident page bytes round up to page boundaries and can slightly exceed logical file size.
file_cache_evidence.rss_overlap_note: Mapped model RSS and filesystem cache describe overlapping physical pages and must not be added.

measurement_protocol.generation_window: First received content/reasoning text event through response completion, not an exact backend-internal decode boundary.

interpretation: The tested model is already read from resident RAM through the OS file cache; a low non-cache-used figure is not evidence of an empty RAM working set.
All six generation windows have zero measured backend physical reads and zero major faults. Avoiding physical disk reads cannot explain a RAM-disk generation gain in these specific windows.
Small reads during initialization and before the first text event were retained; their file identities were not traced and are not assumed to be model-weight reads.
A RAM disk would allocate from the same host RAM and may duplicate cached pages or crowd out inference allocations; tmpfs can also be swapped.
No full-model RAM-disk copy is justified by these warm-control results. If sustained physical reads recur, capture the exact model, resolved backing device, phase, faults and memory pressure first.
limitations: This does not reproduce the user's historical UI observation or establish behavior for every model.
The controls were cache-warm; no cold-load versus RAM-disk end-to-end comparison was performed.
Process physical-read counters do not identify which files were read and do not represent all device-wide activity.
Endpoint memory snapshots do not establish peak usage or safe allocation headroom.
Stream-event observation has overhead and can lag backend computation; no acceleration multiplier is claimed.
These checks establish neither numerical equivalence nor answer quality of the experimental hybrid engine.
recommendation: Retain ordinary file-backed caching for now and return optimization effort to measured CPU/GPU execution and stage-aware prefill. Revisit RAM staging only after reproducing a sustained storage-bound workload, including copy cost and memory pressure.
